summary: Horace Geoffrey Quaritch Wales worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He was educated at Charterhouse School and Queens' College, Cambridge, and served as Field Director for the Greater India Research Committee from circa 1934 to 1941.

Horace Hayman Wilson was an Indologist. He worked for the East India Company, served as Assay Master at the Kolkata Mint, was Boden Professor at Oxford (1833–1836), and held posts at the East India Company College and Royal Asiatic Society.

Horace L. Friess worked in philosophy and religious studies. He studied at Columbia University and Heidelberg University, and later held posts at Johns Hopkins University and Columbia University, where he was attested as professor in 1970.

Horst Lasic specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned his PhD from the University of Vienna in 1999, served as a research fellow at the Austrian Academy of Sciences in 1995, and became a lecturer at Vienna in 1999.
Hoseok Leigh works in philosophy and religious studies. He studied under Ha-u Kim and earned a PhD from the California Institute of Integral Studies (attested 2010).
Hoshu Mitsuhara was a Buddhist studies scholar who served as a professor (attested 1982) and later as professor emeritus (attested 2004) at Koyasan University.

Houn Jiyu-Kennett worked in Buddhist and religious studies. She studied at Durham University and trained under traditional teachers Sek Kim Seng (circa 1961–1962) and Keidō Chisan Kohō (circa 1962–1963).

Hoyo Watanabe is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Rissho University from circa 1952 to 1961. He later served as a Buddhist studies professor (circa 1974–2004) and dean of Buddhist studies (attested 1984–1985) there.
Hozen Seki worked in Buddhist studies. He founded the American Buddhist Academy and served as resident minister at the New York Buddhist Church (attested 1998).

Hsiang-Kuang Chou worked in sinology and Buddhist studies. Having studied under Swami Sivananda, he held posts at the University of Delhi, University of Allahabad, Lal Bahadur Shastri National Academy of Administration, and Yoga-Vedanta Forest Academy.

Hsiao-Lan Hu worked in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. Hu earned a PhD from Temple University and served as associate professor of Religious Studies & Women's and Gender Studies at the University of Detroit Mercy (attested 2017).

Hsing Yun worked in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied under Yin Shun and at the University of Hong Kong, founded Fo Guang Shan and University of the West, and held a post at National Taiwan University.
Hsiu-hui Ji is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed an MA at Fo Guang University under the supervision of Kirill Solonin (attested 2009).

Hsu-feng Lee is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a master's degree at the Chung-Hwa Institute of Buddhist Studies under Huimin and a PhD at the University of Sydney under Mark Allon (attested 2017).

Hsuan Hua was a Buddhist studies figure who studied under Hsu Yun in 1948. He founded the Buddhist Text Translation Society, Dharma Realm Buddhist University, and Institute for World Religions, and served as Abbot of the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas.
Hsueh-li Cheng was a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies who held posts at Ohio University and the University of Hawaii at Hilo (circa 1974–2011).

Hu Shih was a scholar of philosophy, sinology, and history and archaeology. He studied at Cornell, Columbia, Teachers College, and National University, and held posts at Peking University, Fu Jen Catholic University, and Academia Sinica.

Huai-Chin Nan worked in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and sinology. He studied at the Republic of China Military Academy and under Huanxian Yuan, later serving as Professor of Philosophy at Chinese Culture University (attested 1986).

Huaiyu Chen works in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and sinology. He earned a master's at Peking University under Xinjiang Rong, studied under Stephen F. Teiser, and was an assistant professor at Arizona State University (circa 2007–2013).

Huanhuan He specializes in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology. He has held positions at the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences, the University of Tokyo, and Zhejiang University, where he was attested as professor in 2015.
